Abstract: Computational drug repositioning relies increasingly on biomedical knowledge graphs to integrate heterogeneous data sources. However, conventional graph representation learning methods often struggle with representation collapse when handling dense biomedical networks. To address these challenges, this paper proposes Graph-JEPA, an architecture tailored for self-supervised representation learning on heterogeneous biomedical graphs. The framework utilizes a two-layer Relational Graph Convolutional Network (RGCN) encoder and a multi-tasking predictor module to capture complex interactions among biomedical entities in the latent space. By applying an Exponential Moving Average (EMA) target encoder update alongside dynamic edge masking, Graph-JEPA effectively avoids representation collapse without relying solely on negative sampling. The model is trained on a merged knowledge graph combining literature-derived hypotheses from SemMedDB with clinically validated indications from RepoDB. The primary contribution of this study is adapting the Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) to heterogeneous biomedical graphs to mitigate representation collapse without negative sampling. On a held-out test split, Graph-JEPA achieves 78.40% ROC-AUC and 56.17% accuracy, outperforming classical baselines while maintaining latent space stability. Furthermore, a case study on lung carcinoma demonstrates the model’s capacity to infer hidden relational hierarchies, successfully identifying structural suitability for multi-hop candidates such as Etoposide, Gemcitabine, and Entrectinib. The findings establish Graph-JEPA as a robust data-driven decision-making system for advanced drug repurposing tasks.

Abstract: Multi-agent trajectory prediction—i.e., predicting the future positions of a set of interacting agents from their observed motion history—is a fundamental task in autonomous driving, robot navigation, and intelligent surveillance systems. Nevertheless, they usually optimize a per-coordinate reconstruction objective that is sensitive to observation noise and does not reflect the latent cause-effect dynamics in human social interactions. On the other hand, generative approaches with diffusion or flow matching models offer great prediction diversity at the expense of prohibitive inference costs. We present a novel trajectory prediction framework that integrates the Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) paradigm into multi-agent motion forecasting. Unlike conventional methods that predict solely in the coordinate space, our method employs a Social Masking mechanism, which randomly masks the past observations of chosen agents at training time, allowing the model to predict hidden trajectories based on the observed behavior of surrounding agents in a learned latent space. This agent-wise masking imposes a causal inductive bias that forces the network to infer relational information by interacting with other agents, rather than just predicting trajectories based solely on individual agent motion. We use a unified spatio-temporal transformer that simultaneously takes in both past and future frames as a single grid of tokens, without requiring an encoder-decoder stage. A Multi-Modal Decoder with learnable mode queries generates diverse future trajectory hypotheses. Experiments on the NBA SportVU dataset demonstrate that our method consistently achieves state-of-the-art performance, while maintaining highly competitive computational efficiency.
